items.followUp: Compare Rutherford’s and Bohr’s atomic models, including how each explains atomic stability.

rubric.why: Identifies the central nucleus common to both models.
rubric.how: State that both models contain a small, dense nucleus.

rubric.why: Identifies the motion of electrons around the nucleus in both models.
rubric.how: State that electrons revolve around the nucleus.

rubric.why: Contrasts Rutherford’s unrestricted orbits with Bohr’s definite energy levels.
rubric.how: Explain that Rutherford did not propose fixed energy levels, while Bohr placed electrons in fixed orbits or shells of definite energy.

rubric.why: Shows how Bohr’s stationary orbits addressed the stability problem in Rutherford’s model.
rubric.how: Explain that Rutherford’s orbiting electrons would radiate energy, whereas electrons in Bohr’s fixed orbits do not radiate energy.

rubric.why: Credits Bohr’s model with explaining line spectra through definite energy changes.
rubric.how: State that electrons absorb or emit definite amounts of energy when moving between orbits, explaining line spectra.

modelAnswer: Both Rutherford and Bohr proposed that an atom has a small, dense nucleus with electrons revolving around it.
Rutherford did not propose fixed orbits; electrons could revolve at any distance from the nucleus.
Bohr proposed that electrons revolve only in fixed orbits or shells, each with a definite energy.
In Rutherford’s model, revolving electrons should radiate energy and fall into the nucleus; in Bohr’s fixed orbits, electrons do not radiate energy.
Bohr explained line spectra by proposing that electrons absorb or emit definite amounts of energy when they move between orbits.

items.followUp: Define physical chemistry and biochemistry, and state one use of each.

rubric.why: Defines industrial chemistry by its focus on large-scale chemical manufacture.
rubric.how: Define it as the branch concerned with manufacturing chemicals and useful products on a large scale.

rubric.why: Gives an example of a product made through industrial chemistry.
rubric.how: Name a product such as fertilizers, medicines or cement.

rubric.why: Defines analytical chemistry through identification and composition analysis.
rubric.how: State that it identifies substances and determines their composition or the amounts of their components.

rubric.why: States a practical use of analytical chemistry.
rubric.how: Give testing purity or quality control as a use.

modelAnswer: Industrial chemistry is the branch of chemistry concerned with the manufacture of chemicals and useful products on a large scale.
It is used to manufacture products such as fertilizers, medicines and cement.
Analytical chemistry is the branch of chemistry concerned with identifying substances and determining their composition or the amounts of their components.
It is used to test the purity of materials and for quality control.

items.followUp: Discuss four factors that affect the rate of diffusion in gases.

rubric.why: Connects increased temperature with faster particle motion and diffusion.
rubric.how: Explain that higher temperature increases particles’ kinetic energy and speeds up diffusion.

rubric.why: Identifies concentration difference as affecting the rate of diffusion.
rubric.how: State that a greater concentration difference increases the rate of diffusion.

rubric.why: States the effect of particle size on diffusion.
rubric.how: Explain that smaller particles generally diffuse faster than larger particles.

rubric.why: Describes how the liquid medium’s viscosity affects diffusion.
rubric.description: Nature or viscosity of the liquid
rubric.how: State that diffusion is faster in a less viscous liquid and slower in a more viscous liquid.

modelAnswer: Temperature: Raising the temperature increases the kinetic energy of particles, so they move faster and diffusion becomes faster.
Concentration difference: A greater concentration difference between two regions increases the rate of diffusion.
Particle size: Smaller particles generally diffuse faster than larger particles.
Nature of the liquid: Diffusion is faster in a less viscous liquid and slower in a more viscous liquid.

rubric.why: Identifies inorganic chemistry as a branch concerned with elements and their compounds.
rubric.how: State that inorganic chemistry studies elements and their compounds.

rubric.why: States the usual distinction between inorganic chemistry and organic chemistry.
rubric.how: Explain that inorganic chemistry deals with substances other than most carbon compounds.

modelAnswer: Inorganic chemistry is the branch of chemistry that studies elements and their compounds, other than most carbon compounds studied in organic chemistry.
